plan_needed: Claude Free or any paid plan, plus an active Xero subscription. On Claude Team or Enterprise, an Owner must add the connector for the team first (see claude-team-owner-adds-xero).

steps.where: Claude (claude.ai or the desktop app), Customize
steps.do: Go to Customize > Connectors and click the + button next to Connectors. Xero's own page also links straight to the Xero listing in Claude's directory.
steps.see: The connectors directory opens.

steps.do: Click Xero, read its description, then click Connect.
steps.see: You're asked to sign in to Xero.

steps.do: Sign in with your usual Xero login.
steps.see: Xero asks which organisation to connect.

steps.do: Choose the Xero organisation you want Claude to read.
steps.see: You're returned to Claude with Xero connected. The exact Xero approval screen wasn't in the docs we could read.

steps.do: Click + (lower left) or type /, hover over Connectors, and check Xero is switched on.
steps.see: Xero is available in this conversation.

steps.do: Ask about profit, cash, invoices or customers, for example who owes you money.
steps.see: Claude answers from live Xero data, read-only, with links back to the Xero report, invoice or contact it used.

plan_needed: Claude Team or Enterprise, Owner or Primary Owner role.

steps.do: Go to Organization settings > Connectors and click Browse connectors at the bottom of the page.
steps.see: The list of available connectors.

steps.do: Select Xero and click Add to your team.
steps.see: Xero becomes available to the team. Nobody gets access automatically.

steps.do: Optionally set each tool or category to Always allow, Needs approval or Blocked.
steps.see: Members can't override these settings.

steps.do: Each person follows claude-to-xero and signs in to Xero themselves.
steps.see: Each person sees only what their own Xero login allows.

plan_needed: Any paid Claude plan (Anthropic recommends Team for businesses with more than one person), the Claude Cowork desktop app, and the Xero connector connected.

steps.where: Claude marketplace, Small Business plugin listing
steps.do: Click Install in Cowork.
steps.see: The plugin installs in Claude Cowork.

steps.do: Connect the Xero connector if you haven't already (see claude-to-xero).
steps.see: Workflows that list Xero can read your Xero data.

steps.do: Run a workflow such as /monday-brief or /close-month.
steps.see: The workflow starts in approval mode. Claude drafts and stages the work, and nothing is sent, posted or paid until you approve it.

plan_needed: A ChatGPT account and a Xero subscription. OpenAI says availability depends on your plan and workspace settings, and some workspaces need admin approval. Australian availability not confirmed.

steps.do: Open the Plugins directory and search for Xero.
steps.see: The Xero plugin by Xero Limited appears.

steps.do: Open its details and select the plus button to install it (OpenAI's help centre calls this Install plugin).
steps.see: The plugin installs.

steps.do: When prompted, select Connect, sign in to Xero and approve access.
steps.see: The Xero connection is set up. The exact Xero screens weren't in the docs we could read.

steps.do: Start a new chat. Type @ and choose Xero, or just ask and let ChatGPT pick it.
steps.see: Read-only answers from live Xero data, with links back to Xero.

plan_needed: A paid Microsoft 365 Business or Enterprise account and a Xero subscription. Your IT admin may need to approve the agent. These are Microsoft's general steps; Xero's own steps are in a Xero Central article we couldn't read.

steps.do: Select All Agents.
steps.see: The list of agents available to you.

steps.do: Find the Xero agent and select it.
steps.see: Its details open in the details pane.

steps.do: Select Add. If the button says Request approval, ask your IT admin to approve it first.
steps.see: The agent is added, or an approval request goes to your admin.

steps.do: Sign in to Xero when asked.
steps.see: Not described in the docs we could read.

steps.do: Ask about profit, cash position, receivables or overdue invoices.
steps.see: Read-only answers from Xero, with links to open the report, invoice or customer record in Xero.

steps.do: Open the Integrated apps section and find the Xero agent.
steps.see: The agent's permissions and data access, plus its terms of use and privacy statement.

steps.do: Allow the agent for some or all users, or block it.
steps.see: Users can only use agents the admin allows and that they've installed or been assigned.

plan_needed: A personal Google account signed in to Gemini. Work or school accounts need a qualifying Google Workspace edition, Keep Activity on, and an admin who has enabled the app. Google's general steps; Google's article doesn't name Xero yet, and Australian availability isn't confirmed.

steps.do: In the sidebar, click Customize. If you don't see it, click More first.
steps.see: The Customize page opens.

steps.do: At the top, click Connectors.
steps.see: The apps available to your account and country.

steps.do: Find Xero and click Add, then follow the on-screen instructions.
steps.see: Xero is connected. The Xero sign-in screens weren't in the docs we could read.

steps.do: Type @ and select Xero, then ask your question.
steps.see: Answers from live Xero data. Any change, such as issuing an invoice, waits for your explicit confirmation.

from: Xero MCP server (in an AI app such as Claude Desktop)
plan_needed: A Xero organisation in Australia, New Zealand, the UK or the US; a custom connection at $10 a month AUD incl. GST (free on the Demo Company); Node.js 18 or later; some programming experience.

steps.do: Set up a custom connection, choose its permissions (scopes), and enter the email address of the Xero user who will authorise it. If it's for your own business, that's you.
steps.see: Xero emails the authorising user.

steps.do: Open Xero's email and follow it to authorise the connection to the organisation.
steps.see: The connection is linked to that one organisation, and you get a client ID and secret.

steps.do: Purchase a custom connection subscription for the organisation.
steps.see: A recurring monthly charge of $10 AUD incl. GST per custom connection.

steps.do: Install Node.js and add the Xero MCP server to your AI app's local configuration. Keep the client ID and secret only in that local file. Never paste them into a chat or a website.
steps.see: The AI app lists the Xero tools after a restart.

steps.do: Test against the Demo Company first, then ask something simple such as a list of overdue invoices.
steps.see: Read tools return data. Create and update tools change real records, so read every request before you approve it.
